## The World Arrives Through a Face

No one receives a landscape as a landscape-in-itself. The eye receives a
field. The neck gives a direction. The body supplies a boundary. The
ledger records a surface.

A traveler standing on a ridge does not swallow the valley whole. The
valley becomes a view: a center, a horizon, a line of trees, a road that
vanishes at the edge of sight. The valley is not denied. It is disciplined
by a face turned toward it.

This is the first rule of the egocentric interface.

The observer is not a little monarch placed at the middle of the cosmos.
The origin is a gauge, like putting the zero of a map at the station
where the journey begins. It helps the route be read. It does not make the
world orbit the station.

BEDC therefore separates two sentences that ordinary language often
mixes:

```{=html}
<span class="role-tag discovery">⊕ "The readout is centered here."</span>
```

```{=html}
<span class="elim-mark">✗ "The world is ontologically centered here."</span>
```

The first sentence is an interface discipline. The second is a
metaphysical excess. The packet keeps the first and refuses the second.

## The Viewfinder Is Not the Source

A camera does not photograph the entire mountain at once. It has a lens,
a frame, a focus, a falloff of sharpness, an exposure, and a hand that
decides where it points. The resulting image is not fiction. It is also
not the mountain without loss.

The egocentric interface packet treats experience in the same way.

There is a source stage, but the focused history receives it through a
centered frame. There is a support surface, such as a visual disk or some
other finite readout field. There is a clarity kernel: the center may be
sharp while the edge fades. There are attention weights: not every visible
point has the same grip on continuation. There is a classifier: a blur may
be read as a face, a threat, a letter, a shadow, or nothing usable. There
is a ledger: what has entered the history cannot be treated as if it had
never been recorded.

The result is not the bare source. It is a world-for-this-history.

That phrase should be read carefully. It does not mean private fantasy. It
means the source as it has passed through this interface, this attention
surface, this naming regime, this section, this probe policy, and this
ledger. The difference is the difference between a harbor chart and the
sea. The chart is answerable to the sea, but it is not the sea.

## Shaking the Head Changes the Slice

Turn the head and the room changes.

The table does not need to move. The lamp does not need to slide. The wall
does not need to breathe. Still, the frame changes. A corner comes into
view. The window leaves the center. The chair that was a mass becomes a
set of edges. The same source gives a different interface frame because
the readout map has changed.

This is not illusion. It is projection.

A lighthouse beam crossing the same coastline writes different strips of
light at different angles. A scanner passing over the same page sees
different rows at different moments. A sonar cone pointed east and the
same cone pointed west do not deny the sea; they expose different
interface surfaces of it.

The source-fixed scan says exactly this:

```{=html}
<span class="role-tag discovery">⊕ The source may remain fixed while the frame changes.</span>
```

The important point is negative as much as positive. The change in the
experienced frame does not by itself prove that the source changed. It
proves that the source-to-interface projection changed, or that the
classifier can now see a difference it could not see before.

The body, in this reading, is not merely an object inside the scene. It is
part of the route by which the scene becomes recordable.

## Attention Is a Dimmer, Not a Decoration

Attention is often treated as a spotlight. That metaphor is useful, but
too dramatic. Sometimes attention is not a beam. It is a dimmer board.
Every point on the interface has a gain. Some points are turned up. Some
are left almost silent.

Two people may face the same table. One is looking for a lost key. The
other is listening for whether the glass is trembling. The visible frame
may be almost the same, yet the effective read differs. The key-shape has
weight for one history. The vibration has weight for another.

The point is not psychological ornament. It is structural.

The effective read multiplies the rendered frame by a clarity kernel and
an attention weight. When the weight changes at a support point where
something is actually being rendered, the effective read changes. A
written mark can be on the page, but if the reading apparatus gives it no
weight, it does not play the same role in the next continuation.

Attention is therefore not a commentary on experience after the fact. It
is one of the rows through which an interface frame becomes a
world-for-this-history.

## A Thought Enters Like a Seed in the Ledger

Mentation is the delicate part.

An internal event may be small: a question, a remembered face, a fear, a
name, a plan, a suspicion, a wish, a private image. It may not arrive
through the eye. It may not be a fresh external frame. Yet once it enters
the focused history, the ledger is no longer the same.

A compass needle does not move the mountain, but it changes the route. A
margin note does not rewrite the book, but it changes the next reading. A
seed in a field does not instantly become a forest, but the future field
is no longer described by the same packet.

That is the weak but precise claim:

```{=html}
<span class="role-tag discovery">⊕ A ledgered mentation event changes the world-for-this-Hist even when the external source is fixed.</span>
```

It changes the packet because the packet includes the ledger. It may also
change attention, classifier, section, and probe policy. But it does not
need to do all of that for the weak claim. A visible append already
changes the record.

The strictness matters. BEDC does not say that thinking of rain makes the
clouds rain. It says that thinking of rain can change the interface world:
which signs are weighted, which categories are ready, which memories are
called, which probes are selected, and which continuation routes become
available.

## Naming Changes the Door in the Same Wall

Classification is a quiet power.

Before a sound is named, it may be noise. After a name enters, the same
sound may become a warning, a word, an engine, a memory, or an error. The
acoustic source need not change. The classifier row changes how the record
is sorted into future use.

The same is true for section choice.

A compressed interface surface can hide many source-side representatives
behind one public point. A section is a licensed return into that fiber.
Change the section and the same quotient point may carry a different
label. The wall has not moved, but a different door has been opened in it.

This is why the packet includes the section row beside the frame,
attention, classifier, probe policy, and ledger. Meaning is not exhausted
by the visible quotient. Meaning can depend on which certified path
returns from the public surface to a representative in the fiber.

## Intention Chooses the Next Window

Action is not outcome magic.

The hand can choose a lens. It cannot command what the lens will reveal.
The scientist can choose an instrument. She cannot decree the measurement
record. The walker can turn toward the river. He cannot force the river to
be a road.

Probe policy is the row that records this disciplined agency. A focused
history can select the next admissible interface family. It can choose
where to look, what to ask, what to test, which coupling to attempt. But
the next record still depends on the selected interface, the source, and
the outcome kernel.

This preserves intention without making intention a hidden sovereign.
Intention chooses a window. The world still answers through the window.

## The Safe Compression

The dossier can now be compressed without losing the boundary:

```{=html}
<span class="role-tag discovery">⊕ External source fixed; interface world changed.</span>
```

or more sharply:

$$
\Delta X=0,
\qquad
\Delta W\neq 0.
$$

This is not a slogan about mind over matter. It is a ledger statement.
The source component may remain fixed while one visible row of
$W_h=(F_h,A_h,K_h,\sigma_h,\Pi_h,\Lambda_h)$ changes.

The world-for-this-history is like a cockpit display. Outside pressure,
altitude, direction, sensor field, warning lights, pilot attention,
navigation plan, and recorded events all matter. A warning light does not
move the mountain outside the aircraft. Yet once it lights, the world the
pilot must fly in has changed.

That is the philosophical force of the packet: subjectivity is neither a
private mist nor a second substance. It is a disciplined interface
configuration of a finite history.

## Strict Mathematical Form

For a focused history $h$, define an egocentric interface packet
$$
\mathcal E_h
=
(h,C_h,D,a,A_h,K_h,\sigma_h,\Pi_h,\Lambda_h,\mathsf{Aud}_h).
$$

Here $h\in\Hist$ is the focused generated history,
$C_h=(o_h,\Omega_h,B_h)$ is the centered frame row, $D$ is the displayed
interface support, $a:D\to[0,1]$ is the clarity kernel,
$A_h:D\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$ is the attention-weight row, $K_h$ is the
classifier or naming surface, $\sigma_h$ is a licensed section row,
$\Pi_h$ is the probe policy, $\Lambda_h$ is the local ledger, and
$\mathsf{Aud}_h$ is the audit row.

The centering convention is
$$
o_h=0.
$$
This is a gauge row, not an ontological centering of the source.

Let $X_t$ be a displayed source stage and let
$$
\operatorname{Render}_{C_h}(X_t):D\to Y
$$
be the centered readout. Define the interface frame
$$
F_h=V_h(X_t),
\qquad
F_h(u)=
\bigl(a(u),\operatorname{Render}_{C_h}(X_t)(u)\bigr).
$$

When scalar multiplication is displayed, define the effective attended
read
$$
F_h^{\mathrm{eff}}(u)
=
a(u)A_h(u)\operatorname{Render}_{C_h}(X_t)(u).
$$

Define the world-for-this-$\Hist$:
$$
W_h=(F_h,A_h,K_h,\sigma_h,\Pi_h,\Lambda_h).
$$

Experience enters the focused history as an interface frame:
$$
h_{t+1}=\Cont(h_t,F_{h_t}).
$$

A source-fixed scan is a transition satisfying
$$
X_{t+1}=X_t,
\qquad
C_{h'}=g\cdot C_h.
$$

If there exists $u\in D$ such that
$$
a(u)>0
$$
and
$$
\operatorname{Render}_{C_{h'}}(X_t)(u)
\not\sim_Y
\operatorname{Render}_{C_h}(X_t)(u),
$$
then
$$
F_{h'}\not\sim F_h.
$$

Thus a source-fixed scan may satisfy
$$
\Delta X=0,
\qquad
\Delta F\neq 0.
$$

A mentation event is an internal record
$$
n\in\mathcal M_h
$$
with
$$
h'=\Cont(h,n).
$$

Its packet update is
$$
\mathcal U_n:W_h\to W_{h'}
$$
with
$$
\mathcal U_n(F_h,A_h,K_h,\sigma_h,\Pi_h,\Lambda_h)
=
(F_h,A_{h'},K_{h'},\sigma_{h'},\Pi_{h'},
\operatorname{append}(\Lambda_h,n)).
$$

If $n$ is not already present at the displayed endpoint of $\Lambda_h$
and append is visible at the active ledger classifier, then
$$
\Lambda_{h'}=\operatorname{append}(\Lambda_h,n)
\Longrightarrow
W_{h'}\neq W_h,
$$
even when
$$
X_{t+1}=X_t.
$$

If
$$
F_{h'}=F_h,
$$
but for some $u\in D$
$$
a(u)\operatorname{Render}_{C_h}(X_t)(u)\neq 0
\quad\text{and}\quad
A_{h'}(u)\neq A_h(u),
$$
then
$$
F_{h'}^{\mathrm{eff}}(u)\neq F_h^{\mathrm{eff}}(u).
$$

Let $Q_h$ be the compressed interface surface and let
$\sigma_h,\sigma_{h'}:Q_h\to X$ be displayed licensed sections. If a
label row $L:X\to\{0,1\}$ satisfies
$$
L(\sigma_h(q))\neq L(\sigma_{h'}(q)),
$$
then
$$
L_{\sigma_h}(q)\neq L_{\sigma_{h'}}(q),
$$
where
$$
L_\sigma(q)=L(\sigma(q)).
$$

For a displayed action row $a$, if
$$
\Pi_h(h,a)=I,
\qquad
\Pi_{h'}(h',a)=I',
\qquad
I\not\sim I',
$$
then the next admissible probe interface differs. This is probe-interface
selection, not outcome selection by fiat.

The compressed theorem is:
$$
\begin{gathered}
\mathsf{Experience}(h)=F_h,\\
\mathsf{Scan}(X\ \mathrm{fixed})\Longrightarrow \Delta F\ \mathrm{may\ occur},\\
\mathsf{MentationAppend}(n)\Longrightarrow \Delta W,\\
\Delta A\Longrightarrow \Delta F^{\mathrm{eff}},\\
\Delta\sigma\Longrightarrow \Delta L_\sigma,\\
\Delta\Pi\Longrightarrow \Delta I_{\mathrm{future}}.
\end{gathered}
$$

The admissible boundary statement is
$$
\Delta X=0
\quad\text{and}\quad
\Delta W\neq 0,
$$
not
$$
\mathsf{Mentation}\Longrightarrow \Delta X.
$$
